trigger: external-cli-subprocess-dispatch (codex exec argv) + evidence written to a git-tracked, pushed artifact

doubts.claim_under_doubt: adding -c model_reasoning_effort=high is safe for every spec/code/doubt dispatch, because a model or CLI that rejects it makes that codex exec invocation fail at launch, surfacing as status: error, not a silent skip
doubts.disproof_attempt: The claim was asserted three times but verified nowhere; the test carrying it mocks subprocess.run so it can never launch codex. The flag is added unconditionally with no capability guard or degrade path. An operator override to an incompatible model would (per the claim) turn all three required reviews not_run.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Empirically establish the claimed failure mode with a live codex exec call, or add a degrade path, or accept in writing as a deliberate fail-loud trade-off.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: transport_note satisfies the parent spec's bar that evidence records the ACTUAL role, model, effort, sandbox
doubts.disproof_attempt: transport_note is computed before subprocess.run runs -- it is a record of intent, never of observation. The argv decision (codex_review_transport.py) and the evidence decision (transport_note_for in codex_review_roles.py) are two independent evaluations of the same role-in-REASONING_EFFORT_ROLES check; deleting the argv branch alone would leave the note unchanged and no test would catch it.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Add a test tying argv presence of the flag to transport_note's effort= presence for every role.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: moving transport_note construction into codex_review_roles.py is behaviour-neutral and safely documented
doubts.disproof_attempt: Ordering (slug validation before note construction) verified still correct. But transport_note_for's docstring says nothing about the precondition that effective_model must already be validated before reaching it, even though its return value is interpolated into a shell-quoted argument downstream.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: One sentence in the docstring stating the precondition.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: the AC2 fixture's record call is byte-for-byte the same shape codex_review_dispatch.md instructs a production Codex-driven pass to run
doubts.disproof_attempt: Same arguments, not the same path: transport_note is now a 3-word string (spaces), so the doc's --transport-note "{transport_note}" quoting became load-bearing in this same diff. The fixture passes it as a Python list element, which can never exercise shell word-splitting, so it cannot catch a quoting regression.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Make the doc's example unmistakable about the multi-word value and required quoting.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: Test Completeness Ledger row 5: transport_note is the bare model for plan_review, covered by row 6's fixture
doubts.disproof_attempt: Row 6's fixture only loops over spec/code/doubt; plan_review has no --from adapter and is never called by it. No test anywhere asserts run_codex_review('plan_review', ...)['transport_note'].
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Add a test asserting plan_review's transport_note is the bare model.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: the live smoke probe printed reasoning effort: high in its own banner and completed -- the flag is real, in this exact argv position, not merely accepted syntax
doubts.disproof_attempt: The probe as reported placed -c immediately after the subcommand; the shipped code appends -c as the last pair after -o. The probe may also have omitted --ignore-user-config, which would let ambient user config explain the banner instead of the -c override.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Re-run with the exact production argv and paste it into the comment.

doubts.claim_under_doubt: the import-time guards in codex_review_roles.py make the role gate airtight
doubts.disproof_attempt: The gate itself could not be broken. But the subset guard uses assert (stripped under python -O), which the sibling module codex_review_model_resolution.py explicitly documents rejecting for this exact class of guard. The pinning assert on CODEX_REVIEW_REASONING_EFFORT is also tautological.
doubts.what_would_resolve_it: Convert the subset check to raise RuntimeError matching the sibling module's pattern.

summary: 7 doubts (2 high, 4 medium, 1 low). Role gate itself proven airtight; no import cycle from the module move; ordering (validate-then-format) still correct. The two highs -- no capability guard/degrade path on the new flag, and transport_note attesting to an effort setting nobody observed -- are the ones worth real answers.
